Title: There appear to be a few rush guys in G3-4...

Messages.Author: Demnogonis Saastuttaja
Messages.Body:
Posting a lot this week it seems... Well, we have played often and there's a big tournament upcoming.

I just noticed how many POT rush guys there are in G3-4. And in addition to these there would still be Massassi and Jeremy McNeil ADV, who were left out due to not having Animalism nor +Strength.

So the plan goes as follows : devastate your predator, bloat, transfer out more rush guys. Play safe. There's 4 Gustaphes because he's the fastest to transfer out, and 4 Enkidu's because he's the strongest. While you may think it's unrealistic to transfer out every one of them, I'm an optimist and it would be just so cool

It attempts to oust an prey who has no minions left to defend with bleeds. I have had a similar deck with Black Annis and Enkidu that could do that, it just had a pretty different combat that mostly aimed for burning minions and had 10 Flesh of Marbles and 10 Drawings.

The combat module should be obvious. I don't think there's a lot of decks that are safe from that. Well there are some things, such as aggropokes and set range combat end, both which I consider so infrequent I don't care about them.

What else... Nothing I suppose, this is also a deck that I have not tried once. Somehow it seems like such a good idea in my head. Note that just Gustaphe and Enkidu in a situation where you just can't bring out more are still pretty intimidating rush minions.

Messages.Author: Klaital
Messages.Body: 61 combat cards... including 4 manuevers and 8 presses... pretty much anyone with a .44 magnum and handful of celerity can wreck you. Bone Spurs, Fists of Death, and Lids should all be more cards that help you get to close range. Like change lids to slams, an bone spurs and fists to mighty grapples for example. That aside, I don't really see how this deck can survive any half decent predator. Unless you draw that single info highway to start, you will most likely get your first guy out by turn 3, and second at turn 5 or 6. You also have no multiacting for your fatties, so even if you somehow do manage to survive your predator, you would have to go full backwards while your prey runs over the table.

Messages.Author: Pascal Bertrand
Messages.Body:
14 IGs and 8 Lids? It's either long range or close range, you can't have both, and you probably won't be facing 22 rounds of combats with this deck.

Remove the Codex. It's probably the easiest way of getting your guy burned to AI.

Add some Drawing out the Beast / Terror Frenzies. That'll shut the CEL decks down (guns or Richter)

Messages.Author: Demnogonis Saastuttaja
Messages.Body:
Mh, yeah, let's rather have Claws. But about that maneuver thing, Enkidu and Black Annis can use Swallowed for maneuver, and generally this deck deals five damage from long range. Thrown Sever Lid is a choice that stems from from the experience that no amount of maneuvers will be enough. Think about Sniper Rifle, Cailean, why not even Assamites...

I don't know what's a half-decent predator in your books, if the metagame would be full of weenie S&B then sure, but from my last experiences with Enkidu/Black Annis deck I think the concept is viable. My perception of the metagame (local or tournament) is that it's so fatty heavy I don't worry about weenie decks.

I can't worry about AI of all things

A lot of times I have found that I don't want Slam in my hand, but Thrown Sever Lid.

I can't focus more on Karsh, he can't rush most of the best minions in the game

Hm. Could you do such a deck based around multiple monsters? Multirush that has to draw an archetype to work, hm.
